svg.title: Unified Beryl thread navigation concept
svg.desc: An exploratory design board showing merged thread toolbar chrome, a conditional branch-lineage strip, and one shared thread palette in open-existing, new-elsewhere, and rebind-current modes.
svg.text: One Thread Palette · three explicit intents
The selected thread owns runtime/root. The window never switches location independently of opening, creating, or rebinding a thread.
No lineage strip and no reserved empty height.
The same toolbar plus a conditional lineage strip
Ancestors navigate; current segment is passive. Hidden entirely for top-level threads.
THE SAME FLYOUT SHELL, OPENED WITH DIFFERENT INTENT
Recent-first across every runtime and root.
→ Windows roots → Threads in selected root
Only the upper results region changes. The runtime section stays put.
Thread rows activate immediately; this mode has no Confirm footer.
This is a selector, so an existing-thread row is the action. Runtime/root is
only an optional catalog scope, never a separately committed window location.
Rename, pin, archive, delete, and Change runtime/root live behind the header
action menu. Choosing Change runtime/root reopens this palette in rebind mode.
The one-click path stays one click
The primary New Thread segment never opens this flyout. It creates or reuses
an eligible empty thread at the selected thread’s existing runtime/root.
The secondary path is deliberately explicit
Rows only choose the pending target. The bottom section contains nothing except
Confirm, which creates/reuses and activates a thread at that target.
It replaces Recent targets with a runtime’s exhaustive virtualized root list;
Runtimes & roots remains visible, and Back to recent restores the prior view.
Beryl redesign · changes future execution, not Syndic history.
The title and intent change, but root search, recent targets, runtime browsing,
Add root, Add runtime, selection, cancellation, and Confirm remain identical.
The current target is visibly marked and cannot masquerade as a change. Confirm
applies only the highlighted destination after availability gates succeed.
Why this is not in the toolbar
Rebinding is thread metadata maintenance, not ordinary navigation. Keeping it in
current-thread actions prevents a fourth persistent toolbar control.
The flyout does not become a hierarchy-first selector.
Recency remains the default; Browse roots temporarily replaces only the upper working set.
New / rebind mode → select it for Confirm
